14.0.0.en: Judith continued her speech by laying out a plan for the salvation of her people. She was not content with strengthening their faith, then sacrificing herself to destroy Holofernes, then proclaiming his death to them; now she gives them guidance as a military commander on how to attack the Assyrians and finish them off.

14.0.1.en: She is a symbol of the Church, which confirms faith through her Holy Sacraments, overthrows Satan by the Cross of her Christ, leads us in spiritual striving through the various spiritual practices, and teaches us through her saints how to triumph over Satan.

14.0.2.en: Her plan was based, first, on hanging the head of Holofernes on the wall of the city. This is a strong psychological motive, confirming that the victory has been accomplished by her hand, so that the fighting soldiers trust that the victory begun by the hand of Judith will be completed by their striving in the power of God. Likewise the Church hangs the Cross on high before the eyes of the faithful as proof of Christ's victory over Satan, and so urges her children to strive against the wars of the devil.

14.0.3.en: Do not rejoice in your first victory over Satan; rather, for your victory to be completed and to be a true victory, you must continue your striving. The cutting off of the head of Holofernes had to be completed by attacking the Assyrians, to drive them completely away from Judea; that is, you must continue to pursue every evil thought and everything related to sin, so that all your senses are purified. Your striving continues throughout your life, and you will rejoice in the full crown of victory in the Kingdom. For the devil exploits your sense of security and your somewhat lax state after your first victory, to fight you fiercely. So be watchful in order to overcome him, and trust that God supports you to defeat him.

14.1.0.en: The second step in the plan is that they take up their weapons at sunrise and go down from the city, but not quietly like fugitives, or like infiltrators stealing a little water, but with force and loud voices. Thus the Assyrians, whose officers have not yet recovered from the drunkenness and revelry of the previous night, will be taken by surprise by the sight of the army of the Jews, with their swords gleaming in the light of the sun, the mighty voices and the fearsome charge, and they will be confused, alarmed and even terrified.

14.1.1.en: May you attack the devil with your spiritual weapons, which are prayers, the Holy Bible, the sacraments of the Church and every spiritual practice, so that his soldiers are alarmed and are defeated before you. Let your war be at sunrise, early, and you will find God, and He will give you victory over the devil with ease. Do not be afraid of the devil, but attack him with all courage. St. Anba Anthony spoke truly when he said: "The demons are cowards, and they attack only cowards like themselves."

14.2.0.en: Judith told the men of war that if they attacked the Assyrians, their spies who were watching the city of Bethulia would hasten to inform the commanders of the army, who would run to the tent of Holofernes and find him slain. Then the Assyrians would be terrified to find their great, mighty commander, who was thought impossible to kill, slaughtered in the midst of his guards, and they would flounder like sheep without a shepherd, and would hasten to flee from before you.

14.3.0.en: Then she charged them to pursue the Assyrians and run after them, so that they would flee and then be quickly defeated, afraid of the Jews, and she strengthened their faith so that they would follow them up and drive them far away from their land. From this precise plan, in addition to what Judith did with Holofernes and what was mentioned in the previous chapters, we understand that she had certainly seen all this by divine revelation, which encouraged her, and it was her faith that supported her to carry out God's plan, especially since the plan she has just mentioned was fulfilled in all its details - as will appear in the following verses. This confirms that she speaks with the voice of God, confident of what she saw and heard from God. She is like Moses the prophet, who spoke with God, and God gave him not only the commandments and the Law but also the design of the tabernacle in its precise details, and he carried it out according to the pattern he had seen.

14.3.1.en: When you raise the Cross before the wars of the demons, you show them their chief, the devil, bound by the Cross, so they fear and flee from you. So continue in your striving, pursuing them, to drive them out of all your thoughts and senses, and far away from all who are around you, through your service and your care for the souls around you. Trust that God is with you; so be strong and complete your striving, to triumph over them and drive them far away.

14.4.0.en: His foreskin: that is, his uncircumcision; what is meant is that he was circumcised.

14.4.1.en: The custom of the Gentiles: idol worship.

14.4.2.en: Before the mighty work of God by the hand of Judith, Achior felt that there is no god but Him, because He had overcome the strongest personality in the world at that time, Holofernes. So he declared his faith in the God of Israel, and reminded the elders of Bethulia of their promise to him to receive him with them into the faith. He asked to become a Jew like them and to be circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, declaring by the cutting of his flesh that he would cut off idol worship and all the evils of the Gentiles, and that he would live in purity and uprightness before God. After the victory over the Assyrians, he brought his family from the children of Ammon, and he and his household joined the people of the Jews.

14.4.3.en: The power of God at the hands of the saints draws the souls of those who are far off, so that they declare their faith and leave their evils, being baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, they and their households, as happened in the days of the Apostles.

14.4.4.en: Most people are moved by powerful events, such as the wonderful works of God in His saints and His miracles, but few are those who turn their emotional response into faith and faith into deeds. Achior, being moved by what he saw by the hand of Judith, declared his faith, was circumcised and joined the Jews, he and his household. It is not enough for you to be moved by the stories of the saints; you need to strive as they did and follow their example.

14.5.s.en: (2) The discovery of the killing of Holofernes

14.5.0.en: When the day broke: when the day lit up, that is, at dawn.

14.5.2.en: The men of Bethulia carried out the words of their military leader Judith with great precision. At dawn, when the light of day appeared, they hung the head on the wall, then took their weapons and rushed against the camp of the Assyrians with shouting and a great uproar.

14.6.0.en: The spies of the Assyrians hurried to the tent of Holofernes and told the guards of the tent what had happened. But none of them could go in to wake him, or even clap before his tent, because of his greatness and tyranny. So they made a noise and began to speak in loud voices at the door of the tent, hoping that he would wake up, so that they might tell him what had happened.

14.6.1.en: The blessing of obedience is very great, and the humble carry it out with all precision. So did the men of Bethulia, and the events followed one another as Judith had told them. May you be obedient to the Church, to your father of confession and to your spiritual guides, so that you succeed in your spiritual wars and see with your own eyes what God has promised you. Holofernes, this arrogant man whom no one dared to wake, lies on the ground, drowned in his blood, his head taken off him. Bow your head in humility, and God will lift you up; but if you exalt yourself, He will crush you, as the Virgin said in her hymn: "He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree" (Lk 1:52).

14.7.1.en: Their confinement: from "confinement," the meaning being the siege in which the city of Bethulia had been placed by the Assyrians.

14.7.2.en: The news spread quickly among the tents of the Assyrians, especially among the commanders of the armies. All the senior officers of the army gathered before the tent of Holofernes and noticed that the loud voices which the guards were making did not wake Holofernes. With the mentality of guardsmen, they ordered the guards to go in and wake Holofernes so that he might act quickly in the face of this attack coming from Bethulia. Their pride clearly appears, for they described the Jews not as despised human beings, nor even as animals, but as mice that had come out of their confinement; and they did not say "to attack us," but "to provoke us," that is, to try to stir us up, that we might perhaps be willing to fight them.

14.7.3.en: They commanded that Holofernes be awakened, but how can one wake the one who has drowned, whom lust made lose his head, and who has fallen to the ground with his blood flowing? This is the man absorbed in the lusts of the world: he cannot hear the voice of God and be roused from his evil, because he has sunk down to material lusts, so he does not wake up, while he is dying every day without knowing it.

14.7.4.en: Do not despise others if you are strong, and do not exalt yourself because of your abilities, lest your shame appear and God humble you by the weakest of His children.

14.8.1.en: He wailed: he cried out in grief.

14.8.2.en: At the orders of the commanders of the armies, the chief of the guards of the tent of Holofernes - Bagoas the eunuch - went into the reception room, adorned with gold and precious stones, but it was empty, with no one in it. He stood before the cloth curtain that separates the reception room from the bedchamber (the curtain), and heard no sound. He thought that Holofernes, after fulfilling his desire with Judith, had fallen asleep with her, so he was ashamed, and also afraid to go in on them.

14.8.3.en: Because of the tension of the situation, he was forced to disobey the orders of Holofernes by clapping his hands, but no one answered him. He began to suspect that his master was ill or in some distress, so he was forced to lift the curtain and enter the bedchamber. And the surprise came: the body of the strongest man in the world, lying on the ground without a head, and blood around it. He could not control his nerves; he cried out with a great and sorrowful voice and tore his clothes in dread and terror.

14.9.0.en: Had thrown into confusion: shook them and made them troubled.

14.9.1.en: Then he went out quickly, with the eyes of the guards and the commanders of the armies watching him eagerly, and he entered the tent of Judith, pitched beside the tent of Holofernes, and found no one in it. By this he was certain that Judith was the killer of Holofernes. He went out to all the commanders and guards who had gathered, disturbed and eager to know what Holofernes had said, and announced to them that Judith the Hebrew had shaken the Assyrian empire and made it tremble, for she had killed the chief of the armies of the Assyrians, and behold, his body lay headless on the ground in his bedchamber.

14.9.2.en: If you do not heed God's warnings to you, you will be surprised by death before your eyes and will cry out in great fear. Let no one despise your youth or your weakness, for God is able to work through you, like Judith, so that He shakes the greatest nation in the world and subdues under your hands all the powers of evil.

14.10.0.en: When the commanders of the armies heard the news of the killing of Holofernes, it was like a thunderbolt on their hearts. They were terrified, tore their clothes and trembled, for the news was beyond their imagination and conception, and they stood afraid and stunned. Meanwhile the news spread quickly among the tents of the Assyrians, and they were all alarmed and wept with loud cries, not only for the great Holofernes, but for themselves, for they expected destruction like his, by the hand of the God of Israel, whom none can resist, as Achior had told them before.

14.10.1.en: Where is the strength of the strong? It has collapsed before the power of God. Truly, "the Lord shall have them in derision, and vex them in His sore displeasure, and dash them in pieces like a potter's vessel" (Ps 2:4, 5, 9).

14.10.2.en: You can escape terror before God the just Judge through repentance. Instead of weeping without hope at the end of days, offer the tears of repentance and enjoy God's forgiveness in the sacrament of confession.

14.10.3.en: The pursuit of the Assyrians and the plundering of their spoils

15.0.s.en: (1) The pursuit of the fleeing Assyrians

15.0.0.en: They sought help in defeat: accepting defeat became a rescue for them, so that they might flee from the children of Israel and not be killed like their commander.

15.0.1.en: When the news of the killing of Holofernes reached the soldiers of the Assyrians, they lost all ability to think, fear settled in their hearts, and they felt weak and defeated before the God of Israel.

15.1.0.en: While they were afraid and stunned, they bowed their heads in fear and humiliation, and found nothing to say to one another, from the horror of the surprise. When they heard the voice of the Jews coming against them, with their weapons gleaming in their hands, their terror increased. So they fled, leaving behind all their baggage, their tents, their sheep, their cattle and all their possessions, and hurried into the surrounding deserts, taking refuge in all the winding roads between the hills, hoping they might hide them from the face of the people of God. Perhaps the disturbing surprise made them stumble about, and opinions and orders conflicted, so that they scattered without order; some of them may even have fallen dead by the hand of a brother, or been trampled under foot. "Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?" (Ps 139:7). The Assyrians fled from the face of God, but His people overtook them. They killed many of them, and many fell on the way from exhaustion.

15.2.0.en: Making a noise: making a great uproar.

15.2.1.en: Their heels: the heel is the back of the foot, and what is meant is "behind them."

15.2.2.en: When the people of Bethulia saw the Assyrians fleeing, they remembered the words of Judith. They hurried after them, shouting with loud voices, asking for the power of God to support them, and blowing the war trumpets to announce their victory.

15.3.0.en: In one mass: all at once, or as one body.

15.3.1.en: They poured down upon them in a rush like one powerful projectile aimed at them, which increased the fear and alarm of the Assyrians, so that they scattered in confusion in every direction, which made it easy for the Jews to overtake them and kill them.

15.3.2.en: Sin makes a person lose his peace, and when he is troubled he falls into greater sins, until he destroys himself by his own agitation. Be strong, take courage, be strengthened, and let your faith be firm, and Satan will not prevail over you.

15.4.3.en: Then Uzziah, the ruler of the city, moved - as a military commander - to play his part behind Judith. He sent messengers to all the cities of Judea to inform them of the news of their victory over the Assyrians and to urge them to pursue them, to kill as many of them as possible, so that the Assyrians, after their flight, would not try to gather their forces and attack the Jews again. So they quickly chose their brave men and went out armed, in large numbers, from all the cities of Israel, to pursue the Assyrians and kill everyone they overtook, and the Assyrians hurried to flee far away from all Judea.

15.4.4.en: "Behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!" (Ps 133:1). For they support one another on the way of spiritual striving. So all the men of the cities of Israel cooperated in pursuing the Assyrians, to receive the blessing of spiritual striving and victory over Satan. In the Church, among your brethren the faithful, you are strengthened in your striving and grow in your love for God, so that you can overthrow all the thoughts of the enemy and he flees from you quickly.

15.4.5.en: God allowed this so that the people of Bethulia would not be exposed to pride, by feeling that they alone had defeated the Assyrians, but so that the glory would be to God through all His people. Involve others with you as much as you can in prayer, in every spiritual work and in service, so that they receive a blessing from God with you and you are commended. Be like Uzziah, rousing hearts to pursue the way of spiritual striving. And respect the abilities of others with humility, so that you receive the blessing of all.

15.4.6.en: Show your need of those around you, perhaps by this you will encourage them, especially within the one family, between husband and wife and between brothers, and not only from children to parents, but from parents to children. Thus you encourage the faint-hearted and gladden hearts, and then you praise everyone with love and appreciation.

15.5.0.en: They were enriched: they became wealthy.

15.5.1.en: When the Assyrians fled and moved far from Bethulia, the rest of its inhabitants went out to gather the great spoils which the Assyrians had left in their tents: gold, silver, clothing, furniture and many belongings. For the Assyrians carried with them all the needs they required for travel over long months, so these tents were like permanent houses, because the Assyrians had conquered many peoples and taken from them countless spoils, and their tents were full of spoils. They also left behind large flocks of sheep and cattle and all the beasts. As for the men of war from Bethulia, when they returned to their city they carried spoils from the camp of the Assyrians, as much as they were able to carry, so all the inhabitants of Bethulia became rich.

15.5.2.en: Thus the little city of Bethulia became very great, and became the richest of the cities of Israel, and from it came the savior of all the people of God, that is, Judith. She is a symbol of Bethlehem, from which came Christ, the Savior of the whole world, of which the prophets testified, saying: "And thou Bethlehem, in the land of Juda, art not the least among the princes of Juda: for out of thee shall come a Governor, that shall rule my people Israel" (Mt 2:6). God is wonderful, who makes the rich poor and the poor rich. Everything the Assyrians had gathered of wealth and glory they lost in one day, and even lost their lives, because they relied on their own strength. But those who trusted in God endured affliction to the end, and began to fall from thirst and were near death and in great poverty, and their great God turned their mourning into joy and their poverty into limitless riches. Blessed is the one who trusts in You, O Lord; truly in the day of evil You deliver him and lift him above his enemies, and enrich him from Your riches, and he rejoices and praises You.

15.5.3.en: Support me, O Lord, that I may not faint under the pressure of affliction, but trust in You and persevere in my prayers, confident that You do not forget me, and that You will surely give me victory over my enemies, rescue me from every sin and enrich my life with every virtue, so that my heart may meditate on Your praise.

15.6.0.en: When the news of the victory over the Assyrians spread throughout Israel and Jerusalem, the great priest Joiakim, or Eliakim, came from Jerusalem, with the priests and elders of the Jews who lived in Jerusalem, to Bethulia, to meet the great saint Judith, by whose hand God saved His people.

15.7.0.en: When they arrived at Bethulia and entered the house of Judith and saw her, they rejoiced greatly and blessed her, glorifying God, declaring to her that she had become the cause of the glory, joy and pride of all the Jews by this deed of hers, that is, the killing of Holofernes.

15.8.1.en: They praised her courage and strength, as well as the steadfastness of her faith in facing the mighty Holofernes and killing him, in addition to her love of purity and chastity, for after her widowhood she devoted herself to worship; therefore God supported her and completed the victory for her. She is great and blessed, not only in this life, but also for ever in heaven.

15.9.0.en: After Joiakim and his elders had said these words, all the people present at this reception confirmed all that they had said, with confidence, strength and joy.

15.9.1.en: In this way the Fathers, the bishops and the patriarchs, sought the blessing of the saints in the deserts. And even now the Church glorifies her children the martyrs and saints throughout the ages. Your taking part in the celebrations and glorification of the saints rouses your heart to pursue the way of God and kindles your love toward Him. You are a member of the Church; everything good that you do is ascribed to her, and likewise every evil that you commit stains her brow. So try to gladden the heart of your mother the Church, that she may be proud of you.

15.10.s.en: (2) Plundering the spoils of the Assyrians

15.10.0.en: The people of Bethulia - joined by some soldiers of the Jews from the other cities, returning from the pursuit of the Assyrians - continued carrying the spoils from the tents of the Assyrians, which numbered tens of thousands. Each tent had a separate dwelling, full of precious things, not only of what they had taken from Assyria, but even more of what they had plundered from the nations they had occupied.

15.10.1.en: The people of Bethulia carried the spoils to their houses, then returned to carry a second and a third time, and they continued like this for more than a month, gathering each day from the abundant spoils of the camp of the Assyrians.

15.10.2.en: The blessings of God to His children are very many, as the Scripture says: "The blessing of the LORD, it maketh rich, and he addeth no sorrow with it" (Prov 10:22). God is rich; He has much without limit and wants to give to you. What matters is that you hold fast to your sonship to Him and seek His Person, that is, the Kingdom of God, that it may reign over your heart; then He gives you the rest of your needs, that is, all material things, in great abundance.

15.11.0.en: As for Judith, all the people were searching for any means to honor her. While they were plundering the spoils, they gathered everything in the tent of Holofernes and the other tents pitched beside it, in which his belongings were, such as vessels of gold and silver, that is, all his treasures, and presented them to Judith as a gift of love, in gratitude for her kindness and in honor of her deed.

15.11.1.en: The saints who fled from material things and honor and became strangers to the world have been greatly honored by God throughout history, and He has bestowed gifts upon them abundantly, not only on earth but even more in heaven. And when we are raised to heaven on the last day, the places that were emptied by the fall of the demons will be filled by the holy children of God, just as Judith was given the tent of Holofernes, that is, his dwelling.

15.12.0.en: Harps: plural of harp, a stringed musical instrument.

15.12.1.en: When all hearts in Bethulia were filled with joy, the young men and women hurried to the house of Judith, and the women surrounded her, and each one carried whatever musical instruments were common at that time, namely lutes and harps, to sing and chant to God and to honor their great heroine Judith.

15.12.2.en: Do not forget to thank God for the works of His care for you every day in your prayers and your praises. And do not neglect also to honor everyone who deserves honor, with kind words and by every means, so that you rejoice and gladden hearts: "honour to whom honour" (Rom 13:7). Thanking God and the greatness of Judith
